query: How do I type exact influence and speed values into the After Effects Keyframe Velocity dialog to reproduce a cubic-bezier ease like 0.05, 0.7, 0.1, 1?
must_contain: Opens Keyframe Velocity (Animation > Keyframe Velocity / Ctrl+Shift+K) and explains Incoming vs Outgoing Velocity with Speed and Influence fields
Relates influence % to how far the bezier handle reaches in time and speed to the handle's slope (units/sec), i.e. how a bezier x/y maps onto those numbers
Notes that multi-dimensional non-spatial properties (Scale, color) carry a separate ease per dimension, while spatial Position has a single ease along the path
why_we_need_it: SML tokens are cubic-beziers and the assembler applies them as AE influence/speed through kumo keyframe.set_easing, so the mapping must be exact.

query: In After Effects, how do I make a position move overshoot slightly and settle by separating dimensions and pulling bezier handles in the value graph?
must_contain: Right-click Position > Separate Dimensions to get independent X/Y value curves (and why the combined speed graph cannot overshoot)
Value-graph technique: drag the outgoing/incoming bezier handles so the curve passes beyond the target value and returns, or add a settle keyframe
Keeping the overshoot small/felt rather than bouncy, and keeping X and Y timing in sync after separating
why_we_need_it: SML says overshooting tokens (ease.out, y1>1) must go on separated dimensions because AE clamps overshoot on spatial Position.

query: Why does my layer's motion path curve or loop past the keyframes in After Effects, and how do I make spatial interpolation linear by default for UI and text moves?
must_contain: Distinguishes spatial interpolation (path shape in the comp) from temporal interpolation (speed/ease in the graph editor)

Auto Bezier / Continuous Bezier spatial keys create curved or overshooting paths; fix via Keyframe Interpolation dialog (Spatial: Linear) or Preferences > General 'Default Spatial Interpolation to Linear'
Shows that linear spatial keys still keep their temporal easing
why_we_need_it: Our AE comp defaults require linear spatial keys for type and UI moves; drifting curved paths break card and chip layouts.

query: How do I animate text per character in After Effects with a text animator and range selector so letters rise and fade in with a staggered, eased cascade?
must_contain: Add Animator > Position + Opacity, then animate Range Selector Offset or Start; Based On characters/words
Advanced settings: Shape (Ramp Up / Smooth), Ease High / Ease Low, and how they control the per-letter ease and overlap
How the selector's duration relates to the stagger (e.g. total cascade length), optionally Randomize Order
why_we_need_it: AE-native titles must follow SML stagger tokens (stg.1 letters, stg.2 words, cascade cap 500 ms) so they cut with builder-made type.

query: How do pros sync word-by-word kinetic typography to a voiceover in After Effects so each word lands on the spoken word and still looks premium, not template-like?
must_contain: Practical sync method: audio waveform (LL), layer/comp markers on spoken words, then aligning word reveals to markers (separate layers or text animator Based On words)
Design guidance: one hero word with strong scale/weight contrast, restrained secondary words, readable hold times
Timing nuance such as having the graphic lead the word by a few frames rather than lag it
why_we_need_it: Our lectures and tech videos are VO-driven, and graphics must lead their keyword by 0.05–0.6 s per the tech-canvas style.

query: How do I animate a rounded-rectangle UI card in After Effects so it resizes without distorting its corner radius or stroke width (shape Size vs layer Scale)?
must_contain: Animate the Rectangle Path Size (and Position) inside the shape group instead of layer Scale, so Roundness and stroke stay in pixels
Keeping the card anchored to an edge or corner while it grows (anchor point / position offset or a simple expression)
Optional: linking a child layer (content, shadow, mask) to the card's size so they stay aligned
why_we_need_it: Presenter and screen cards morph between full, strip, large and corner states, and stretched corners look amateur.

query: How do I make a clean line draw-on animation for connector lines, arrows or icons in After Effects with Trim Paths, rounded caps and good easing?
must_contain: Trim Paths Start/End (and Offset) keyframing, plus Trim Multiple Shapes: Simultaneously vs Individually for staggered draws
Stroke settings: round line cap/join, stroke width, and adding an arrowhead or dot that follows the path end
Easing the draw (ease-out on the leading end) and avoiding a linear robotic look
why_we_need_it: Leader lines from muse's mitten, pipeline diagrams and rings are drawn as strokes in AE overlays.

query: What After Effects expression adds a damped spring or inertial bounce after the last keyframe, using the keyframe's incoming velocity?
must_contain: Working expression code using nearestKey/numKeys, velocityAtTime and a decaying sine (amplitude, frequency, decay parameters)
Explanation of what each parameter does and how to tune for a subtle versus playful settle
Note on applying to multi-dimensional properties, and/or converting the expression to keyframes (Convert Expression to Keyframes)
why_we_need_it: SML spring tokens are built in AE as expressions, then converted to keyframes before handoff.

query: After Effects expression to move layers along a tilted elliptical orbit around a center null, scaling them up when in front and down when behind to fake depth
must_contain: Expression using Math.cos/Math.sin with time, radius and period, with the y radius squashed by the tilt (R*sin(tilt)) and rotated by a roll angle
Tying scale, opacity or blur to sin(angle) so near items are bigger and far items smaller, plus a phase offset per layer (index or a slider)
How to pass items behind a subject: splitting into front/back copies, a matte, or true 3D layers with a camera
why_we_need_it: The approved memory-atom FX orbits muse on tilted rings that pass behind and in front of him.

query: How do I set up depth of field with an After Effects 3D camera so foreground and background layers blur realistically, with focus linked to a layer?
must_contain: Camera Settings: enable Depth of Field, Focus Distance, Aperture/F-Stop and Blur Level, and how they interact
Link Focus Distance to Layer (or an expression that measures the distance to a target layer) so focus follows the subject
Spacing layers in Z for believable falloff, plus a renderer note (Classic 3D vs Advanced 3D / Cinema 4D) or the performance cost
why_we_need_it: Premium AE looks (particle depth, bokeh behind the host, 3D worlds) depend on camera DOF that the browser builders cannot do.

query: How do I make a smooth premium parallax camera push-in on 2.5D layers in After Effects using a null-parented camera, without a floaty or drifting feel?
must_contain: Rig: one-node camera (or two-node camera with point of interest handled) parented to a null, animating the null rather than the camera
Z spacing for parallax and scaling distant layers to compensate their apparent size
Easing the push (strong ease-out with a long tail or ease-in-out) and avoiding sub-pixel jitter or uneven speed
why_we_need_it: Camera moves are hero motions that use ease.move.emph and dur.7, and AE owns 3D camera depth in our engine split.

query: Motion blur is not showing on my precomp or nested comp in After Effects; which switches need to be on inside and outside the precomp?
must_contain: The layer motion blur switch must be on for the animated layers inside the precomp and for the precomp layer itself, with Enable Motion Blur on in each comp
How the shutter angle/phase and samples come from comp settings (Advanced tab), and how Collapse Transformations changes the behaviour
That footage or PNG sequences with motion baked in get no blur from the layer switch (that needs Pixel Motion Blur or RSMB)
why_we_need_it: The assembly nests slot comps inside the main comp, and our default is 180°/−90° blur on every comp.

query: How do I add motion blur to an already-rendered PNG sequence in After Effects with RSMB or Pixel Motion Blur, matching a 180-degree shutter and avoiding edge artifacts on alpha?
must_contain: Applying RSMB (or stock Pixel Motion Blur) to footage and setting the blur amount or shutter so it equals 180° (e.g. 0.5 blur amount)
Handling transparent footage: RSMB Pro foreground/alpha settings or blurring in a precomp over transparency to avoid smearing the background
Fixing vector artifacts: tearing or warping on fast or overlapping motion, vector smoothing, motion-vector quality
why_we_need_it: Fast builder footage arrives without blur, and RSMB 6 is installed for exactly that case.

query: What Deep Glow settings give a realistic, physically based glow on neon text or UI in After Effects without blowing out the whole frame?
must_contain: What the main Deep Glow controls do (Radius, Exposure, Threshold, Falloff/Quality, Tint, Chromatic Aberration) with starting values
Isolating the glow source (glow on a duplicate or alpha-only layer, then composited back) so backgrounds and white text do not bloom
Bit depth note: 16 or 32 bpc for smooth falloff, and how exposure behaves in 32 bpc
why_we_need_it: Deep Glow 2 is our main premium plugin, and it only beats stock glow with an alpha-isolated source.

query: Why does my glow disappear on a white or light background in After Effects, and how do I make a glow or halo read on light backgrounds?
must_contain: Explains that additive or screen glow cannot brighten pixels that are already white, so the halo vanishes
Fix: a coloured, darker or saturated halo composited Normal (or Multiply/Color Burn variants) that extends the alpha, rather than an additive glow
Practical recipe: a glow pass on an isolated layer, tinted, with opacity or falloff tuned, possibly with a subtle shadow for contrast
why_we_need_it: Muse's lectures sit on a white keynote cyc, and the memory-atom FX needed halos that read on white.

query: How do I make premium glowing particles orbit or trail around a character in After Effects with Trapcode Particular, with a stock CC Particle World fallback?
must_contain: Particular setup: a light or layer emitter following a path or null, Particle size/opacity/color over life, and an Aux system for trails
Depth: using the comp camera for DOF and bokeh, and keeping particles out of the subject's face zone with masks or emitter placement
A stock fallback route (CC Particle World / CC Particle Systems II, or expression-driven shape layers plus glow)
why_we_need_it: The approved 'around muse' FX uses particles and orbits, and every plugin recipe needs a stock-AE fallback.

query: How do I build a smooth zoom or whip-pan transition between two scenes in After Effects with matched easing and directional blur, without plugins?
must_contain: Structure: precompose each scene, animate scale or position across the cut with an ease-in into the cut and an ease-out after it
Hiding edges with Motion Tile (Mirror Edges) and adding Directional Blur or motion blur peaking at the cut frame
A typical duration in frames and keeping the move direction consistent between the outgoing and incoming shots
why_we_need_it: SML treats a transition as the scene's exit (one primary type plus 1–2 accents), and AE builds them at assembly.

query: How do I make a card-expand or shape-mask reveal transition in After Effects where the next scene appears inside a growing rounded rectangle, using track mattes?
must_contain: Track matte setup (Alpha Matte / the newer track matte layer picker) with a shape layer as the matte above the incoming scene
Animating the matte's Size/Roundness (not Scale) with ease.move-style easing, and optionally moving the outgoing scene with it
Finishing touches: a soft shadow or stroke on the card edge, and avoiding a visible matte edge or aliasing
why_we_need_it: Layout morphs between presenter-card states and screen cards are our most common transition in the tech-canvas style.

query: How do I stop banding in dark gradients and glows after H.264 export from After Effects by working at 16 bpc and adding grain or noise dither?
must_contain: Why 8 bpc and H.264's 4:2:0 compression cause banding, and that working at 16 or 32 bpc alone is not enough once you deliver 8-bit
Adding grain/noise (Add Grain, Noise, Fractal Noise overlay) at a size and amount that survives compression
Export tips: bitrate, avoiding a second lossy encode, and checking banding on the final file
why_we_need_it: The ident finish adds grain against banding in dark gradients, and all our comps are 16 bpc going to MP4.

query: How do I composite a cut-out character onto a clean studio backdrop in After Effects so it sits in the scene, with a contact shadow, cast shadow and light wrap?
must_contain: Cast or contact shadow from the layer's alpha: a black fill, skew or corner pin onto the floor, blur increasing with distance, low opacity
Light wrap: blurred background composited onto the subject's edges through its alpha (a stock method or Light Wrap effect)
Edge and colour match: matte choke/feather and matching blacks, colour temperature and saturation to the plate
why_we_need_it: Muse is composited onto a white keynote cyc with cast shadow, reflection and light wrap in AE.

query: When importing a PNG sequence with alpha into After Effects, how do I set straight vs premultiplied alpha and the frame rate so there are no dark fringes or timing drift?
must_contain: Import as an image sequence, then Interpret Footage: Alpha Straight vs Premultiplied (Matted With Color) and what Guess does
Symptoms of the wrong interpretation (dark or white halos on edges) and how to fix them
Setting 'Assume this frame rate' to the comp fps so frames map 1:1, and why a mismatch causes skipped or duplicated frames
why_we_need_it: Our footage contract is PNG sequence, straight alpha, same fps, and every builder clip enters AE this way.

query: Why does my imported ProRes 4444 or PNG footage look washed out or colour-shifted in After Effects compared with the source, and which colour management settings fix it?
must_contain: Project working space and colour management settings (none vs sRGB/Rec.709, linearize working space) and their effect on blending
Interpret Footage > Color: embedded profile vs Preserve RGB / override input profile
Known ProRes gamma or matrix issues (Rec.601 vs Rec.709 tagging, QuickTime gamma) and how to verify a match
why_we_need_it: We require a non-linear working space and bt709/sRGB, and we have hit the ProRes 601 tagging bug before.

query: Why does my precomp look pixelated or soft when scaled above 100% in After Effects, and when should I use Collapse Transformations or Continuous Rasterization?
must_contain: A precomp rasterizes at its own comp size, so upscaling it in the parent resamples pixels
Collapse Transformations (precomps) and Continuous Rasterization (shape, text, vector layers) keep vectors sharp, with their side effects on blend modes, effects order, masks and 3D
Alternatives: build the precomp at the needed resolution, or apply the zoom inside the precomp
why_we_need_it: Screen cards and boards get auto-zooms (×1.11–1.25 and ×2 pushes) on nested comps, and text in them must stay crisp.

query: How do I render a long After Effects comp reliably from the command line with aerender, using frame-range chunks, memory flags and output module templates, then join the parts?
must_contain: aerender flags: -project, -comp, -s/-e frame range, -RStemplate/-OMtemplate, -output, -mem_usage, -mp/-continueOnMissingFootage
Splitting into chunks or separate processes to avoid memory growth and slowdowns, with an image sequence or intermediate codec for safety
Joining chunks without re-encoding or frame errors (e.g. image sequence then one encode, or a concat with matching settings)
why_we_need_it: Long 16 bpc renders with Deep Glow ran out of memory and slowed to 0.4 fps, so studio ae render needs chunked aerender runs.
